text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today, pulling back from a three-day rally that had pushed the stock up to $142.28 on November 13th. The decline came as crude oil prices softened slightly—US oil dropped to $89.62 per barrel from levels that had been supporting the recent upward momentum. After a 4% drop over the past two weeks, the stock appears to be consolidating rather than breaking down decisively.

The energy sector remains buoyed by elevated heating oil prices (up 59% year-over-year) and steady refinery economics, which should continue to support oil majors. However, with crude prices now sitting in a narrower range and no major company-specific news in the past few days, the stock lacks a fresh catalyst to extend its recent gains.
